$description: Byte strings the boundary check MUST reject. `failure` names a CodecError.failure (the four-part check); `code` names a ReaderError.code raised by @dagsocial/wire itself. A vector here that starts passing means a guarantee was lost.

rejects.name: non-minimal/vlqU-one-padded
rejects.note: ⚠ THE headline case. 0x81 0x00 decodes to 1 exactly as 0x01 does, and @dagsocial/wire accepts it DELIBERATELY (WIRE_INTERFACE → 'Two asymmetries are deliberate'). Nothing but step 3's re-encode-and-compare catches it. Delete that step and this vector is the one that stops failing.

rejects.name: non-minimal/vlqU-zero-max-padded
rejects.note: Ten bytes encoding the value 0 — the widest padding MAX_VLQ_BYTES still admits.

rejects.name: non-minimal/vlqU-inside-array-element
rejects.note: Padding on the SECOND element. The compare is over the whole byte string, so a non-minimal field buried mid-struct is caught the same as a leading one.

rejects.name: non-minimal/array-count-padded
rejects.note: The count itself padded: 0x81 0x00 = 1 element. The length prefix is as much a canonicity surface as the payload.

rejects.name: non-minimal/lp-length-padded
rejects.note: A padded zero-length prefix. `80 00` decodes to length 0 exactly as `00` does.

rejects.name: trailing/one-byte-after-vlqU
rejects.note: Step 2. Without the isExhausted assertion, appended junk rides free — and any two byte strings sharing a prefix would decode to one value.

rejects.name: tag/bool-two
rejects.note: Strict tags — no truthy coercion, per TYPES_INTERFACE -> Primitives.

rejects.name: tag/enum8-unknown
rejects.note: Tag 0 is not in the mintReason table. Reserved tags stay unreadable rather than decoding to a neighbour.

rejects.name: tag/enum8-sentinel-byte
rejects.note: The encode-side sentinel must not decode back into a value — otherwise a malformed round trip would look clean.

rejects.name: tag/postType-unknown
rejects.note: Tag 2 is not in the postType table. The closed set is the point — every future post kind is a deliberate protocol decision.

rejects.name: truncated/lp-payload-short
rejects.note: Declared 4 bytes, supplied 3 — a length prefix that outruns the buffer.

rejects.name: overflow/vlqU-eleven-bytes
rejects.note: Past MAX_VLQ_BYTES. Bounds the read loop on a malformed stream.

rejects.name: overflow/vlqU-past-safe-integer
rejects.note: The sentinel's own bytes on the `number` path. It must never decode into a plausible value — that is what keeps the sentinel one-way.

rejects.name: overflow/array-count-past-max
rejects.note: MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH + 1 = 2^24 + 1. Rejected on the count alone, before anything is allocated.

rejects.name: utf8/invalid-continuation
rejects.note: 0xff starts no UTF-8 sequence. A non-fatal decoder would substitute U+FFFD, mapping two distinct byte strings onto one string — decoded lossily, then re-encoded to different bytes.

rejects.name: utf8/truncated-sequence
rejects.note: The first two bytes of a 3-byte sequence, with a length prefix that says the field ends there. The bytes are all present — it is the sequence that is incomplete — so this is a decode fault, not a short read.
